disposition_reason: Primary measurements of Cd, Ni and Pb in fermented, dried Ecuadorian cocoa beans from nine provinces (FAAS and GFAAS, mg/kg fresh weight); Table 2 gives per-province Cd range and mean, text gives selected per-province Ni and Pb means and all-province summaries.

study.design: farm/origin survey (ministry-supplied random samples per province)
study.material_scope: fermented and dried cocoa beans (milled, homogenised); nine provinces, one canton per province (Table 1)
study.growing_origin_vs_market: Grown in Ecuador (Azuay, El Oro, Esmeraldas, Santo Domingo de los Tsáchilas, Manabí, Guayas, Los Ríos, Napo, Bolívar); supplied by MAGAP's National Fine Flavor and Aroma Cacao and Coffee Reactivation Project; not market samples
study.sampling_unit: analytical preparations: 6 FAAS + 3 GFAAS per province sample entry (9 provinces x 9 = 81; 243 metal observations). Number of independent field lots per province not stated (Table 1 lists one entry per province).
study.method: Microwave acid digestion (HNO3 70% 5 mL + H2O2 30% 3 mL, 180 °C), FAAS and GFAAS (PerkinElmer AAnalyst 400); reference method IPN AC-06-00
study.lod_loq: LOQ FAAS: Cd 0.25, Ni 7.5, Pb 7.5 mg/kg; GFAAS: Cd 0.0125, Ni 0.125, Pb 0.125 mg/kg. LOD = 3 SD of blank, numeric values not reported.
study.basis: fresh weight (as stated: 'All the results are presented in mg·kg-1 of fresh weight'); material is fermented and dried beans, milled and homogenised; moisture not reported, no dry-weight conversion
study.qa: Spike recoveries with CRM standards: FAAS Cd 91.2 ± 2.9%, Ni 89.6 ± 2.3%, Pb 97.6 ± 1.3%; GFAAS Cd 98.7 ± 4.7%, Ni 99.3 ± 3.5%, Pb 101.1 ± 12.4%. Replicate RSD 5.0-11.4%. INEN interlaboratory proficiency test on cocoa beans, z = 0.97 and -0.42. No matrix CRM. t-test: no significant FAAS vs GFAAS differences.

controls.control: Cocoa variety (CCN51 vs Nacional vs blends) as a Cd/Ni correlate
controls.comparator: Province samples of differing variety (Table 1); variety fully confounded with province (one entry per province)
controls.outcome: Authors note some of the highest Cd was in CCN51 (Guayas 1.73, Los Ríos 0.89 mg/kg, Table 2 means) and some highest Ni in blended samples (Esmeraldas 8.528, Manabí 6.033 mg/kg), but state they 'could not establish a relationship between the metal concentration and the variety'. Not usable as a varietal effect estimate.

controls.control: Cd as a proxy for Ni and Pb screening
controls.outcome: No linear relationship between metals: R2 0.027 (Cd-Ni), 0.242 (Cd-Pb), 0.121 (Ni-Pb); PCC 0.215, 0.36, 0.360; VIF 1.03, 1.32, 1.14. Implies a Cd result does not predict Ni or Pb in these beans.

regulatory.instrument: Regulation (EU) No 488/2014 (as cited by the authors)
regulatory.product: chocolate <30% total cocoa dry matter / 30-50% / >=50% ; cocoa powder
regulatory.locator: Introduction p4 lines 78-86; values 0.1, 0.3, 0.8 mg/kg and 0.6 mg/kg cocoa powder as cited (context only; verify against the regulation itself)

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary calls 0.267-1.715 (Cd), 0.502-1.966 (Pb), 1.462-8.528 (Ni) the 'range' of bean concentrations; in the primary these are the ranges of province means. Preparation-level Cd extremes in Table 2 are 0.24-1.75 mg/kg.

Stored summary says 33.3% of samples 'exceeded EU threshold of 0.80 mg/kg' and calls it a 'bean-equivalent threshold'; the 0.8 mg/kg EU/Codex value applies to chocolate with >=50% total cocoa dry matter, not beans. The paper's highlight only says Cd >0.8 mg/kg in 33.3% of samples.
Stored summary says province-level data were not extracted and sample size is not stated; the primary has Table 2 per-province Cd (n=9 preparations each, 81 total) and Table 1 provenance.
Stored summary omits that results are on a fresh-weight basis (as stated) and that FAAS LOQ for Ni and Pb (7.5 mg/kg) exceeds nearly all reported Ni/Pb values.
Stored summary's limitation that 'FAAS used for Cd has lower sensitivity' omits that GFAAS (Cd LOQ 0.0125 mg/kg) was also used for three of nine preparations per province.
unresolved: Per-province Ni and Pb means for the five provinces not named in the text (Ni: El Oro, Guayas, Los Ríos, Napo, Santo Domingo de los Tsáchilas; Pb: Azuay, Bolívar, El Oro, Los Ríos, Manabí) are shown only as box plots (Figs 2-3) without numeric labels; not digitised.
Per-preparation values are not printed; no sample_values available.
Whether the ± values in the text are SD (mg/kg) or RSD (figure captions say '± RSD') is not stated explicitly; recorded as SD because printed in mg/kg.
Why Table 2 Cd means differ slightly from the Results-text means (e.g. Guayas 1.73 vs 1.715) is not explained.
Fresh-weight basis of fermented, dried beans: moisture not reported, so comparison with dry-weight bean data carries unknown (likely small, ~5-8% moisture) basis difference.
